name: Citus
model: A Postgres extension that makes a cluster: distributed tables sharded across workers, small reference tables copied to every node
engine_note: Ordinary Postgres on every node (heap plus B-tree; optional columnar access method); a coordinator plans queries and routes them to shards
consistency: Single-node transactions get normal Postgres guarantees. Multi-node transactions are atomic via two-phase commit but have no distributed snapshot isolation: a query can see a concurrent commit on one node and not yet on another. Worker replicas are Postgres streaming replicas, so they can lag.
scaling: Sharding by a distribution column you choose (for example tenant id); add worker nodes and rebalance shards online; queries run in parallel across workers.

licence_events.event: Citus 11.0: all former enterprise features (such as non-blocking shard rebalancing) open-sourced, so the whole extension is under the AGPL.

managed: Azure Database for PostgreSQL elastic clusters
Azure Cosmos DB for PostgreSQL (on a retirement path)
reach: Reach for it for multi-tenant SaaS on Postgres where each tenant's data fits on one node, or for fast parallel analytics over large Postgres tables.
avoid: Avoid when transactions often span many shards and need consistent snapshots, or when one Postgres server is still enough.
escape: You leave the Postgres default for this because one Postgres server is too small but you want to stay on Postgres.
chat: Messages and usage events sharded by tenant or user id when one Postgres server can no longer hold them.
notes: Transaction semantics quoted from the Citus technical README (main branch): 2PC atomicity, no distributed snapshot isolation. Microsoft Learn (updated 2026-04-27) says Azure Cosmos DB for PostgreSQL is on a retirement path and not recommended for new projects; use Azure Database for PostgreSQL elastic clusters (Citus inside). The 2022 blog says 'fully open source' without naming the licence; the LICENSE file on main is AGPL v3. Citus is owned by Microsoft (acquired 2019).
